sections.title: Market Pulse: Hawkish Fed Comments Pressure Wall Street on Friday

items.headline: Major Indices Close Lower on Friday Following Fed Chair Warsh's Hawkish Stance
items.summary: U.S. equities concluded Friday's trading session in negative territory as investors reacted to Federal Reserve Chair Kevin Warsh's hawkish remarks at the Jackson Hole Summit, which intensified expectations for a September interest rate hike. Despite the daily declines, all three major indices managed to secure weekly gains. The market's advance, however, exhibited narrow breadth, with Big Tech maintaining significant sway. Not financial advice.

items.headline: Intel Jumps on Positive Sentiment
items.summary: Intel ($INTC) surged 9.49% on Friday. The move comes amid continued investor focus on large technology stocks.

items.headline: Tesla Gains Ahead of Week's Close
items.summary: Tesla ($TSLA) climbed 3.80% by market close on Friday, contributing to the strength seen in some 'Magnificent Seven' stocks.

items.headline: Amazon Rises Amid Tech Sector Focus
items.summary: Amazon ($AMZN) advanced 3.71% on Friday, as large-cap tech continued to influence overall market performance.

items.headline: Marvell Technology Crashes Despite Positive Outlook
items.summary: Marvell Technology ($MRVL) plummeted 10.3% on Friday, despite reporting upbeat quarterly earnings and raising its outlook. The decline was attributed to the expected payoff from its custom AI chip deal with Google being pushed out to fiscal 2029.

items.headline: Nvidia Retreats After Earnings-Driven Rally
items.summary: Nvidia ($NVDA) fell 4.6% on Friday, paring some of its significant gains from Thursday. The decline was due to profit-taking following its strong Q2 earnings report and a hawkish shift in Fed policy expectations.

items.headline: AMD Slips as Chipmakers Face Selling Pressure
items.summary: Advanced Micro Devices ($AMD) dropped over 2% on Friday, as the semiconductor sector experienced selling pressure following broader market volatility and Fed comments.

sections.title: Market News: Jackson Hole Sparks Rate Hike Concerns, Tech Divergence

items.headline: Fed Chair Warsh's Hawkish Jackson Hole Speech Drives Rate Hike Expectations
items.summary: Federal Reserve Chair Kevin Warsh delivered a hawkish speech at the Jackson Hole Summit on Friday, reiterating the central bank's commitment to the 2% inflation target and offering no indication of impending interest rate cuts. This address significantly increased market expectations for a 25-basis-point rate hike at the upcoming September FOMC meeting, with probabilities rising to 57%. The hawkish stance led to a hardening of bond yields, with the two-year U.S. Treasury yield climbing to 4.34%.

items.headline: Technology and Communication Services Lead Weekly Gains Amid Market Divergence
items.summary: For the week ending August 29, Communication Services (+1.43%) and Technology (+1.30%) were among the leading sectors. However, Friday's session saw small caps and semiconductors facing the largest losses, highlighting a divergence in market performance where major indices gained but broader market breadth was weak. AI and Big Tech continued to exert significant influence on the S&P 500's movements.

items.headline: July PCE Data Shows Modest Inflation Rise, Stalled Consumer Spending
items.summary: Economic data released Friday indicated that the July Personal Consumption Expenditures (PCE) price index rose 0.2% month-over-month and 2.5% year-over-year. The core PCE, excluding volatile food and energy, also increased by 0.2% month-over-month and 2.6% year-over-year. While personal income saw a 0.4% rise, consumer spending notably stalled.

items.headline: Nvidia and Marvell Earnings See Mixed Market Reactions
items.summary: Despite reporting overwhelmingly better-than-expected Q2 earnings on Thursday, Nvidia ($NVDA) saw its shares drop on Friday due to profit-taking and the hawkish Fed outlook. Similarly, Marvell Technology ($MRVL) experienced a significant decline even after an upbeat earnings report and raised guidance, as the market reacted to a delayed payoff from a key AI chip deal.
